samples.summary: After any failed write, the in-memory mirror shadows localStorage for the rest of the session, so later cross-tab changes are silently ignored
samples.evidence: `memoryFormat` is set in `setDateFormat`'s catch (line 72) and only cleared by a *successful* `localStorage.setItem` (line 66). `getDateFormat` returns it unconditionally first (line 48). In an environment where writes keep failing (Safari private mode, exhausted quota, sandboxed iframe) the mirror stays non-null forever, so when the `storage` listener added in `subscribe` (line 79) fires, `getDateFormat` still returns the mirror and the value another tab wrote — or cleared — is discarded. The doc comment on lines 35-37 asserts the opposite invariant ("storage stays the single source of truth"), which only holds once a write succeeds. The new test at tests/lib/date-format-preference.test.ts:104 covers only the succeed-once-then-clear path, not the never-succeeds path.

samples.summary: `readStoredTheme` returns an unvalidated string that is cast to `Theme`, so a junk stored value is applied as an html class and as `resolvedTheme`
samples.evidence: `readStoredTheme` is typed `string | null` and line 65 does `(readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme`. Any non-empty stored value (a stale key, or one written by other code on the same origin) flows into state unchecked and reaches `root.classList.add(theme)` and `newResolvedTheme = theme as ResolvedTheme` (lines 86-87), yielding an arbitrary class on `<html>` and a `resolvedTheme` outside its union. The sibling module added in this change validates the analogous read with `isFormat` (date-format-preference.ts:26,51), and the URL-param path just above (lines 63-64) validates too, so the storage path is the odd one out; this hunk wrapped exactly that read without adding the guard.

samples.summary: The "exact" option's example contradicts its own comment for one week each year
samples.evidence: `sample` is `Date.now() - 7 days`, and the comment on lines 32-33 says it "reads ... exactly as a same-year 'Jul 25'". Between Jan 1 and Jan 7 the sample falls in the previous calendar year, so `formatExactDate(sample)` on line 81 includes the year, showing a differently shaped example than the format recent documents will actually render.

samples.summary: `formatListDate` silently drops its injectable `now` when the format is "relative"
samples.evidence: Lines 144-146: `format === "exact" ? formatExactDate(value, now) : formatRelativeTime(value)`. `now` exists so rendering is testable without the wall clock (comment at lines 104-105), but the relative branch ignores it and `formatDistanceToNow` reads the real clock — a caller passing `now` has it honored for one format and not the other (see tests/app/documents/document-list-utils.test.ts:173, which cannot pin the clock).

samples.summary: Each date cell subscribes to two window events, so a large list installs listeners per row and re-reads storage on every unrelated `storage` event
samples.evidence: `DateCell` calls `useDateFormat()` (line 241) and is used for both the Modified and Created columns (lines 875-876), so an N-row page creates 2N `useSyncExternalStore` subscriptions, each adding a `CHANGE_EVENT` and an unfiltered `storage` listener (date-format-preference.ts:78-79). The `storage` handler never checks `event.key`, so any origin-local key write in another tab wakes every cell's snapshot read (each touching `localStorage.getItem`). Snapshot equality keeps this correct, but the work scales with row count; hoisting the hook to the table and passing the format down avoids it.

finding.summary: `readStoredTheme` result is cast to `Theme` without validation; a junk stored value can throw from `classList.add`
finding.evidence: Line 65: `return (readStoredTheme(storageKey) as Theme) || defaultTheme;`. The new helper hardens the *access* but still returns any string unvalidated. A stored value containing whitespace (e.g. left by an older build, an extension, or a manual edit) flows into the effect at line 87 as `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws `InvalidCharacterError` for a string with a space — an exception thrown from the provider's effect, i.e. the whole app. Any other junk value also silently mislabels `resolvedTheme` via the `theme as ResolvedTheme` cast at line 86. The sibling module added in this same change (`date-format-preference.ts`, `isFormat`) validates; this one does not.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: theme-provider.tsx:65 casts `readStoredTheme(...)` (typed `string | null`, line 25-31) directly to `Theme` with only a falsy check, so any non-empty stored string becomes the theme state. At lines 86-87 any value other than "system" is passed to `root.classList.add(theme)`, which throws InvalidCharacterError for a token containing whitespace — inside the provider effect that wraps the entire app (App.tsx:73) — and `theme as ResolvedTheme` at line 86 mislabels resolvedTheme for every useTheme() consumer on any junk value. I searched for a guard and found none: writeStoredTheme (line 33) is the only typed writer, the postMessage path validates ("light"/"dark", lines 118-120) but the storage read does not, and the sibling module added in the same change does validate (date-format-preference.ts:26,51 `isFormat`). Reachability requires a foreign/legacy localStorage value, which lowers likelihood but not impact; no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.
